Nodes.name: Gap grows with training set size
Nodes.description: In diffusion models, the gap between the early timescale (\tau_{gen}) and the later timescale (\tau_{mem}) grows as the size of the training set increases.

Nodes.name: Timescales emerge under n < n*(p)
Nodes.description: The two distinct timescales in the training dynamics of diffusion models emerge under the condition n < n*(p).

Nodes.name: Timescales correspond to inverse eigenvalues
Nodes.description: In the random feature setting, the timescales of training dynamics of diffusion models correspond to the inverse eigenvalues of the random feature correlation matrix.

Nodes.name: Generalization timescale scaling
Nodes.description: The characteristic timescale where high-quality sample generation begins (\tau_{gen}) scales according to the formula \tau_{gen} \propto W^{-1}.

Nodes.name: Memorization timescale scaling
Nodes.description: The characteristic timescale where memorization of training data starts to emerge (\tau_{mem}) scales according to the formula \tau_{mem} \propto nW^{-1}.

Nodes.name: Generalization timescale is constant
Nodes.description: The generalization timescale (\tau_{gen}) remains constant regardless of the training set size (n).

Nodes.name: Memorization timescale increases linearly
Nodes.description: The memorization timescale (\tau_{mem}) increases linearly with the training set size (n).

Nodes.name: Training loss decreases during memorization
Nodes.description: On the timescale where overfitting and memorization occur, the training loss decreases.

Nodes.name: Test loss increases during memorization
Nodes.description: On the timescale where overfitting and memorization occur, the test loss increases.

Nodes.name: Convergence to empirical score at long times
Nodes.description: The training dynamics of diffusion models converge to the low-lying minimum corresponding to the empirical score only at very long training times.

Nodes.name: Low-frequency part close to population score
Nodes.description: The low-frequency part of the empirical score is close to the population score.

Nodes.name: High-frequency part is dataset-dependent
Nodes.description: The high-frequency part of the empirical score is dataset-dependent.

Nodes.name: n-dependent change in loss landscape
Nodes.description: A fundamental n-dependent change in the loss landscape drives memorization in diffusion models.

Nodes.name: Score model not expressive enough when n > n*(p)
Nodes.description: When the training set size n exceeds the threshold n*(p), the score model is not expressive enough to represent the empirical score associated to n data.

Nodes.name: Score model provides smooth interpolation when n > n*(p)
Nodes.description: When the training set size n exceeds the threshold n*(p), the score model provides a smooth interpolation, approximately independent of the training set.

Nodes.name: Larger W achieves generation earlier
Nodes.description: Higher-capacity networks with larger network width W achieve high-quality generation earlier than smaller networks.

Nodes.name: Larger W memorizes earlier
Nodes.description: Higher-capacity networks with larger network width W begin to memorize earlier than smaller networks.

Nodes.name: U-Net base widths W tested
Nodes.description: The U-Net base widths W tested to analyze the impact of model capacity are 8, 16, 32, 48, and 64.

Nodes.name: Total parameter counts p tested
Nodes.description: The total parameter counts p tested to analyze the impact of model capacity are 0.26, 1, 4, 9, 16 \times 10^6.

Nodes.name: U-Net architecture used
Nodes.description: The score model used in the study has a U-Net architecture [46].

Nodes.name: Three resolution levels
Nodes.description: The score model used in the study has three resolution levels.

Nodes.name: Base channel width of W
Nodes.description: The score model used in the study has a base channel width of W.

Nodes.name: Channel width multipliers
Nodes.description: The score model used in the study has channel width multipliers of 1, 2, and 3 respectively.

Nodes.name: Fixed capacity p=4x10^6 used
Nodes.description: A fixed model capacity with parameters p=4\times10^6 was used to isolate and investigate the impact of training set size n on the metrics.

Nodes.name: Fixed capacity W=32 used
Nodes.description: A fixed model capacity with base width W=32 was used to isolate and investigate the impact of training set size n on the metrics.

Nodes.name: Overfitting disappears when n > threshold
Nodes.description: Overfitting disappears even at infinite training times when the training set size n becomes larger than a model-dependent threshold.

Nodes.name: n > n*(p) is architectural regularization
Nodes.description: In the (n, p) phase diagram, the condition n > n*(p) corresponds to the architectural regularization regime.

Nodes.name: Training set size n is a main parameter
Nodes.description: The size of the training set n is one of the two main parameters that define the diffusion model regimes.

Nodes.name: Expressivity is a main parameter
Nodes.description: The expressivity of the class of score functions on which the diffusion model is trained is one of the two main parameters that define the diffusion model regimes.

Nodes.name: Expressivity characterized by p
Nodes.description: The expressivity of the class of score functions on which the diffusion model is trained is characterized by a number of parameters p.

Nodes.name: Empirical score composition
Nodes.description: The empirical score is composed of a low-frequency part and a high-frequency part.

Nodes.name: Irregularity of empirical score drives gap
Nodes.description: At low noise levels and large training set sizes, the irregularity of the empirical score is the key driver behind the widening gap between the generalization and memorization timescales.

Nodes.name: Learning bias towards low frequency
Nodes.description: Deep neural networks exhibit a learning bias towards low frequency functions.

Nodes.name: High-frequency learning time scales with n
Nodes.description: The training time required to learn the high-frequency, dataset-dependent part of the score scales linearly with the training set size n.

Nodes.name: RFNN used to parameterize score
Nodes.description: A Random Features Neural Network [RFNN, 43] is used to parameterize the score function in the study of the training dynamics and timescales of score-based models.

Nodes.name: Timescale formula
Nodes.description: The mathematical formula relating the training timescales of score-based models to the eigenvalues of the random feature correlation matrix is tau^-1 = psi_p/Delta_t lambda_min.

Nodes.name: Gradient descent used
Nodes.description: Gradient descent is the optimization method used to study the dynamics of score learning both analytically and numerically.

Nodes.name: Theorem 3.2
Nodes.description: Theorem 3.2 establishes the emergence of two distinct training timescales in the overparameterized RFNN model.

Nodes.name: Random matrix theory tools used
Nodes.description: Tools from random matrix theory are used to compute the eigenvalue spectrum in the limit of large datasets, high-dimensional data, and overparameterized models.

Nodes.name: SGD optimization used initially
Nodes.description: The theoretical results regarding the training timescales were initially derived under SGD optimization.

Nodes.name: Timescales arise under Adam
Nodes.description: The two key training timescales arise under the Adam optimizer.

Nodes.name: Fewer steps under Adam
Nodes.description: The number of optimization steps required for the two distinct training timescales to emerge under the Adam optimizer is much fewer than under the SGD optimizer.

Nodes.name: Toy Gaussian mixture dataset used
Nodes.description: A toy Gaussian mixture dataset was used to show that the scaling of the memorization timescale with training set size holds in conditional settings.

Nodes.name: Classifier-free guidance used
Nodes.description: Classifier-free guidance [21] was used to show that the scaling of the memorization timescale with training set size holds in conditional settings.

Nodes.name: Implicit dynamical regularization enlarges regime
Nodes.description: Implicit dynamical regularization in training substantially enlarges the generalization regime of score-based generative models.
